recap.text: Carl and Donut's trebuchet, looted from Dream elves, holds about fifty Dazzlers: alarm-and-spotlight traps that strobe the closest enemy's eyes and all play one song. The first of four salvos lands in Louis's craters, and Killing in the Name shakes the ground louder than the explosions. Deshrouded then strips every war protection, ear protection included, but the Dazzlers keep playing. Donut and Mongo scream, and most of the enemy cover their ears or eyes.

beats.headline: Fifty in the trebuchet
beats.text: The army has one trebuchet of its own, a small one Carl and Donut looted from some Dream elves on the sixth floor. It is loaded with about fifty contraptions called Dazzlers, with almost two hundred more piled nearby. They are basically an alarm and a spotlight trap combined: they shine only toward the eyes of the closest enemy soldier, strobing powerful multi-coloured beams into their faces, and they all play the same song at the same time. They are one of the few trap modules Victory allows in a trebuchet.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut load a small looted trebuchet with about fifty Dazzlers, strobing, song-playing spotlight traps.

beats.headline: Killing in the Name
beats.text: The trebuchet fires the first of four salvos, spreading Dazzlers in and around the middle of Louis's craters. The announcement is louder than Carl expects, even from this far away: Justice Light's tips on enhancing them have worked. He slips his earplugs in. They barely help. Peaking at number three on June 20, 2020, despite first coming out in 1992, it's Killing in the Name. The Rage Against the Machine song shakes the ground louder than the explosions, and anyone within a few hundred meters takes immediate, painful hearing damage.
beats.gist: The trebuchet fires Dazzlers into Louis's craters; Killing in the Name wrecks hearing nearby.

beats.headline: Still playing
beats.text: A big one: Deshrouded. The war protections are gone, all of them. The illusions vanish, the smoke clears, and every temporary protection spell snaps off, the ear protection included. The lights and music from the Dazzlers do not turn off. Donut and Mongo both seem to be screaming with pain, and Mongo rears at the sound. For a moment there is an unobscured view across the dim battlefield, where several of the enemy have turned from the painful light and most have their hands over their ears or eyes.
beats.gist: Deshrouded strips every war protection, yet the Dazzlers' lights and music keep hurting Donut, Mongo and the enemy.
